questions.q: An asset fails to depreciate because its category was deleted after the asset was added. Which earlier concept explains this failure?
options: Category integrity, tied to category books from Chapter 2
The prorate calendar's mid-quarter convention
Mass transaction selection criteria
Revaluation reserve accounting
questions.explain: A deleted or invalid category breaks the link to the category book's default depreciation rules, a direct consequence of Chapter 2's category setup concepts.

questions.q: A partial retirement of a multi-unit asset leaves the remaining units with an unexpected net book value. What should be checked first?
options: Whether the asset was revalued
Whether the asset's location flexfield is populated
Whether Create Accounting ran in draft mode
Whether the retirement was entered by cost or by units, and whether the proportional calculation is correct
questions.explain: Lesson 24 covers retiring by cost versus by units; a wrong-looking result after a partial retirement is usually a data-entry error in that proportional calculation.

questions.q: When reconciling Assets to GL and the balances don't match, what should typically be checked first?
options: Whether a batch is simply pending transfer or pending posting (a timing issue)
Whether the asset was retired by mistake
Whether depreciation projections were run
Whether the asset category is too granular
questions.explain: Lesson 31 establishes timing (transfer-versus-post) as the fastest, most common explanation to rule out before investigating other causes.

questions.q: The wrong asset number is retired by mistake during a mass retirement, caught the same week before period close. What is the correct fix?
options: Add the asset back as a brand-new addition with a new date placed in service
Leave it retired and adjust the General Ledger manually
Reclassify the asset into a new category
Reinstate the asset to restore its original identity and depreciation history
questions.explain: Since the retirement itself was the error and it's caught before accounting and period close, reinstatement is the correct fix, not a fresh addition.

questions.q: What is the recommended diagnostic sequence this lesson teaches for troubleshooting a Fixed Assets problem?
options: Symptom, likely cause, the specific lesson/concept explaining the mechanism, then the fix
Always roll back depreciation first, regardless of the symptom
Escalate every issue directly to Oracle support without investigation
Apply a fix immediately, then look for the symptom afterward
questions.explain: The repeatable habit taught across all four scenarios is identifying the symptom, forming a hypothesis about the cause, tracing it to the relevant concept, and only then applying a fix.
